text:
Kiel’s median asking rent sits at 11.27 €/m² in June 2026, up 4.8 % year‑on‑year and 28.8 % over the past five years, placing the city 21st of the 37 most expensive German markets. The asking premium over existing rents is 48 %, with a typical 60 m² unit costing 676 € per month.

The market remains balanced but tight: listings stay on the market for an average of 23 days, only 30 % are let within a week and the vacancy rate is 1.6 %. Rent‑burden for two residents is 16.2 %, while the population grew merely 0.2 % in the last five years.

A model estimate forecasts the median asking rent to reach 11.89 €/m² in 12 months, ranging between 11.61 €/m² and 12.14 €/m², implying a 5.5 % increase.
